speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning, I am Dr. Agent. Can you tell me if you have experienced any headaches, blurred vision, or nosebleeds recently? Additionally, do you have a family history of high blood pressure or kidney disease?

speaker: Patient
text: 5-year-old boy. The patient is presented by his mother for a well-child visit. The boy was born at 39 weeks gestation via spontaneous vaginal delivery, is currently up to date on all vaccines, and is meeting all developmental milestones. His mother reports that he has been generally doing well with no concerns. No family history of cardiovascular disease. The boy does not take any medications.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since your son is 5 years old and we are evaluating for secondary hypertension, do you notice he has become significantly taller or heavier than other children his age recently? Also, does he have a history of urinary tract infections or recurrent sore throats?

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Uric_Acid, Blood_Creatinine, Electrolytes, Renal_Ultrasound.

REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Since the initial labs and abdominal ultrasound are normal, let's focus on the upper body and neck. Can you describe the appearance of his neck and chest? I am specifically looking for signs like an enlarged thyroid, a continuous machine-like murmur, or any visible masses.

REQUEST IMAGES: Neck_Imaging, Chest_XRay.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is High blood pressure on the right upper extremity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
That is a critical finding; please ensure the cuff size used was appropriate for his age and arm circumference. Are there any other blood pressure differences between his arms or legs? Also, does he have a history of congenital heart defects or cyanosis?

REQUEST TEST: Blood_Culture, Cardiac_ECG, Echocardiogram.
REQUEST IMAGES: Cardiac_Imaging.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Blood_Culture: Normal, Cardiac_ECG: Normal, Echocardiogram: Narrowing of the aorta distal to the left subclavian artery with a gradient, consistent with coarctation. Left ventricular function is normal. Cardiac_Imaging: Normal heart size, rib notching not observed (may not be present in young children).

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Coarctation of the Aorta. The combination of unexplained hypertension in a young child, a discrepancy in blood pressure between extremities, and echocardiographic confirmation of aortic narrowing distal to the left subclavian artery is diagnostic. No further testing is required.
